# Generated connector reference

Protocol version: **2**. Generated from [protocol.ts](../../packages/connectors/src/protocol.ts), its imported contracts and the real connector manifest exports. The tables are field summaries; use the [JSON Schema bundle](../protocol/connector-protocol.schema.json) for nested fields, constraints, required properties and unions, and the [OpenAPI document](../protocol/connector-protocol.openapi.json) for the routes. A running Clew serves both, a viewer and a manifest dry run under `/api/protocol` (D60), generated from the same code as these files. Schema validation does not replace [behavioral validation](../guides/testing-and-deployment.md).

The manifest field by field, with examples and the rules between fields, is [manifest-reference.md](manifest-reference.md).

## Complete runnable examples

- [hello manifest](hello.manifest.json), from [connector.mjs](../../connectors/hello/connector.mjs): 5 capabilities; scan enabled.
- [phonebook manifest](phonebook.manifest.json), from [connector.mjs](../../connectors/phonebook/connector.mjs): 5 capabilities; no scan.
- [hr manifest](hr.manifest.json), from [connector.mjs](../../connectors/hr/connector.mjs): 18 capabilities; scan enabled.
- [finance manifest](finance.manifest.json), from [connector.mjs](../../connectors/finance/connector.mjs): 14 capabilities; scan enabled.
- [incidents manifest](incidents.manifest.json), from [connector.mjs](../../connectors/incidents/connector.mjs): 4 capabilities; scan enabled.
- [communication manifest](communication.manifest.json), from [connector.mjs](../../connectors/communication/connector.mjs): 5 capabilities; scan enabled.
- [timesheet manifest](timesheet.manifest.json), from [connector.mjs](../../connectors/timesheet/connector.mjs): 5 capabilities; no scan.
- [payroll manifest](payroll.manifest.json), from [connector.mjs](../../connectors/payroll/connector.mjs): 3 capabilities; no scan.
- [appraisals manifest](appraisals.manifest.json), from [connector.mjs](../../connectors/appraisals/connector.mjs): 4 capabilities; no scan.

These JSON files are complete, generated inputs, not abbreviated pseudocode. They contain no credentials. The [signed walkthrough](../../scripts/docs-smoke.ts) runs the phone book fixture; the [quickstart](../guides/creating-a-connector.md) explains how to adapt it.

## ConnectorManifest

| Field | Required | Shape | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `protocol` | yes | 2 | The version of this contract the manifest is written to, not of the connector (D60). This instance loads 2; an additive change to the protocol keeps the number. |
| `id` | yes | string | Stable and lowercase. Must match the id Clew was configured with, and prefixes every capability name. |
| `kind` | yes | "passthrough" / "derived" | Who owns the data (D3): `passthrough` when it lives in the connected system and Clew keeps refs and audit rows only; `derived` when the connector computes it from other sources. `core` is Clew's own and never a remote connector. |
| `source` | yes | string | Swedish. The system as shown on cards: "Personalsystemet". |
| `areas` | yes | array of object | The areas this connector gives a person: each names and marks the connector's cards, is a choice in Hem's area filter, and holds its standing capabilities, schedules and figure. Where each shows is in docs/guides/where-things-open.md. Empty is allowed for a connector that only answers questions. |
| `capabilities` | yes | array of object | What the connector can do, one entry per operation. The name is the contract (D37): a break is a new name, never a changed one. |
| `uses` | no | array of string | The exact capability names of other connectors this one calls back through `POST /api/connectors/call` while serving a request (D37), such as `calendar.today`. A name not listed is refused; an `execute` can never be called back. |
| `facts` | no | array of object | The fact kinds this connector creates (D55), each prefixed with its id. |
| `scan` | yes | boolean | Whether Clew should POST /clew/scan for each person nightly and on first visit. |
| `delegation` | no | object | The connector acts as the person against its system with a token Clew obtains by token exchange. |
| `documents` | no | boolean | Implements POST /clew/documents for authorised, versioned binary document reads (D79). |
| `header` | no | object | The shared header (D88): this connector can give Clew the header it draws above every page, for the people in the connector's audience, as the content system (Sitevision, SharePoint, WordPress) lists its sections for them. Declaring it makes the connector a candidate, not the holder: only the one connector an administrator chose to give the header answers, whatever the order connectors were registered in. Clew keeps no header of its own beyond its default (the site's name and Start). |

## ManifestCapability

| Field | Required | Shape | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `execution` | no | object, one of `strategy`: "manual" / "deduplicated" / "conditional" | How a write may be repeated safely after a lost answer (D45): `manual`, `deduplicated` (operation ids kept for `retentionSeconds`, found by `lookup`) or `conditional` (`lookup` tells whether the effect holds). Omitted means manual. Only meaningful on an `execute`. |
| `name` | yes | string | `<connector id>.<verb>`, stable. Two names are profiles Clew combines across connectors: `<id>.search` (D26, see `kinds`), and `<id>.errands` (D35, D89), a read that takes `{ view?: "assigned" \| "reported" }` and answers an ErrandsOutput with the errands the case system lets the person see. Its view's `open` names the read that shows one errand, by convention `<id>.errand`. Clew lists every `<id>.errands` in the person's scope as `clew.errands`. A third is combined the same way: `<id>.news` (D112), a read that takes `{}` and answers a NewsOutput with the news the person may read; its view's `open`, when a row should open in Clew rather than by its `link`, names the read that shows one item, by convention `<id>.newsItem`. Clew lists every `<id>.news` in the person's scope as `clew.news`, newest first, on Hem and as "Alla nyheter"; a source that fails contributes nothing. Two more are the talks profile (D96), answered by one system per installation rather than combined: `<id>.talks`, a read that takes `{}` and answers a TalksOutput (the open round of development talks and one row per person the reader manages, keyed on the SCIM `userName`), and `<id>.commitments`, a read that takes `{ person?: <userName> }` and answers a CommitmentsOutput (that employee's action points for a manager of their unit, or without `person` the ones the reader owns and the ones about the reader). `<id>.talks` may be limited to managers; `<id>.commitments` should be callable by everyone who owns action points or is their subject. Clew's built-in `talks` connector answers while either of its reads is enabled for the person; otherwise the one connector whose `<id>.talks` or `<id>.commitments` the person may call does, and with several none does. Neither is ever offered to the model. |
| `kind` | yes | "read" / "propose" / "execute" | `read` answers; `propose` drafts something for a person to decide; `execute` changes the source and runs only after a human decision (D8), never as a tool and never through a callback. |
| `title` | yes | string | Swedish. A button label. |
| `description` | yes | string | Swedish. What the model reads when `model` is true. |
| `input` | yes | object (free keys) | JSON Schema of the input. Clew validates a call against it before the connector sees it. `required` properties mean the capability needs input, which keeps it out of the menu and out of the conformance check's calls. |
| `output` | yes | object (free keys) | JSON Schema of the output. Clew validates the answer against it; where it declares `properties`, a view's keys must be among them (D38). |
| `model` | yes | boolean | Offer it to the model as a tool, once an administrator has enabled tools for the connector. Must be false for execute (D8). |
| `scope` | yes | object | Who may call the capability at all. Omitted roles means every signed-in person. The connector narrows further in the call. |
| `kinds` | no | array of "document" / "person" / "case" / "room" | For `<id>.search` (D26): what it can find. Its output is a SearchOutput; `<id>.fetch` takes one of its refs back and returns one SearchHit. |
| `view` | no | object, one of `kind`: "document" / "metrics" / "activity" / "series" / "record" / "table" / "list" / "detail" / "text" | How Clew draws the output: `table` and `list` over an array of records (`rows`, default "rows"; `title` names the field that names a row and is one of `fields`; `ref` the field holding the connector's ref), `detail` over one record, `text` over one Markdown string. |
| `review` | no | string | On an execute: the same-connector document or record read taking {ref}, whose version-bound evidence is required on approval. |
| `menu` | no | object | How this capability's view is named and marked when an administrator puts it in Clew's menu under Verktyg (D40). Only on a read that declares a view and needs no input. |
| `about` | no | object | What the rows concern (D97). A `read` takes `{ keys }` (an array of at most 200 strings, required) and answers `rows` (or its view's rows), one per key it knows, each with a string `key` it was asked with; a key outside the caller's scope is answered as no row, never as a refusal. It declares a `table` or `list` view, is never a tool (`model: false`), and may answer `heading` and `note`, two strings beside the rows. A `propose` or `execute` names in `param` the input property that takes one key. Clew decides where it shows: an action in the entity's menu, a read as a section on the opened entity, a `warn` or `alert` tone as a mark on its row, a table or list as a lens an administrator may offer. |
| `follows` | no | array of string | For a `propose` (D55): the fact kinds it answers for. Input is a FactEnvelope, output a FollowResponse; steps name this connector only. |
| `creates` | no | string | The fact kind this `propose` or `execute` brings about (D55); must be one of the manifest's `facts`. |
| `asks` | no | array of object, one of `kind`: "meeting" / "text" / "long-text" / "date" / "choice" | On a `propose` or `execute` (D112): what the person fills in before it runs, each naming one property of the input. Clew draws the asks as the first step of the action's dialog, "Fyll i", from every place the action can be started, and merges the answers into the input; the rest comes from the selected rows (`refs`), the action's own `input` on a work item, or the entity (`about.param`). An answer for anything not asked is refused. |
| `effect` | no | string | On an `execute` (D112): a `read` of this connector that takes the same input and answers an `EffectOutput`, what the write will do where, without writing anything. Clew calls it as the person with the input the execute would get and draws the answer as "Det här händer", the last step before anything is sent. Without it Clew names the source and shows the capability's `description`. |

## ManifestArea

| Field | Required | Shape | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | string | Stable and lowercase. Hem's area filter names it in its address (`/?area=<id>`), and a scan draft names it in `area`. |
| `title` | yes | string | Swedish. The area's name: a choice in Hem's area filter and the rail's search, and the word that marks its cards (D71). |
| `roles` | yes | array of "manager" / "employee" | Who sees the area: at least one role. |
| `standing` | yes | array of string | Capability names the area offers, each a capability of this manifest. A propose or execute among them is suggested under "Menar du" while the person types in the question box on Hem; a read among them marks its view with the area's word and icon and has no entry of its own. |
| `schedules` | yes | array of object | What the connector does for this area on its own and when. Informational text that Clew keeps with the manifest and draws nowhere today; the scan itself runs nightly and on first visit. |
| `figure` | no | boolean | Clew asks POST /clew/figure for this area's figure and draws it as a tile on Hem (D54), unless an administrator switched it off. |
| `icon` | no | "phone" / "people" / "book" / "document" / "chart" / "search" / "clock" / "link" / "calendar" / "bell" | One of Clew's icons. The connector sends a name, never a drawing. |

## Actor

| Field | Required | Shape | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | string |  |
| `name` | yes | string |  |
| `unitId` | yes | string |  |
| `unitLabel` | yes | string |  |
| `role` | yes | "manager" / "employee" |  |
| `userName` | no | string | The person's provisioned directory user name (SCIM `userName`, D68): the key your system knows them by, and the key a read about a person is asked with (D97). Absent for a person provisioned without one. |
| `units` | no | array of object | The units a manager follows up (D117): their own, managed or placed on, and those of the managers who report to them (D99). Present on a manager's reads about a person or a unit and on the views they open; a read about a unit may answer for these units and must refuse every other. Absent means `unitId` alone. |
